title: Tech View opens on 13 default columns with small grey header labels
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as {User-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST DC04 Fresh Columns), a user with the Admin role at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) who has never opened Tech View or changed its columns.
  • Your browser window is 1440 px wide, with the browser zoom at 100%.
  • For the steps that name 1536 px, your screen lets you widen the window to 1536 px.
  • The design pictures DC-04-tech-view-header-row-1440.png and DC-04-tech-view-all-columns-1440.png are open beside the app at 100% zoom (actual size); they are attached to this case.
  • In the design pictures the header row starts with a collapse arrow and a position-number column, and two labels read "Unit #" and "Assigned Tech": the first two are left out of this release and the labels follow the PRD (Unit, Assigned Techs), so do not compare those.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST DC04 Dan Columns) is an active technician at {Location-A}.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST DC04 Default Columns") is used by this case only.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17810) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is chosen in any filter, Assigned to me is off, Search is empty and density is Regular (the default).
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Tech View in the display switcher.
  2. Read the column header labels from left to right, scrolling the table sideways to see them all.
  3. Compare the size, weight and colour of the header labels with the row text under them and with the design picture.
  4. Look at the space between each pair of neighbouring header labels.
  5. Click the column chooser button.
  6. Turn on On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician, and every other column the chooser offers that is off.
  7. Press Escape.
  8. Scroll the table sideways from left to right and look at every header label.
  9. Click the density button and choose Compact, and look at the header labels.
  10. Click the density button and choose Comfortable, and look at the header labels.
  11. Widen the window to 1536 px and look at the header labels again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: there are 13 columns, in this order: Status, Waiting On Parts, Number, Customer, Unit, Asset, Progress, Service Advisor, Clocked In, Lines, Assigned Techs, Created on, Total price. On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician are not shown.
  • Step 3: the header labels are small (12 px in the design, visibly smaller than the 14 px row text under them), medium weight (not bold) and grey (lighter than the dark row text), as in the design picture.
  • Step 4: no header label touches or overlaps its neighbour; there is clear space between every pair.
  • Step 6: On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician are offered and can be turned on.
  • Step 8: with every column on, no header label touches, overlaps or is cut off by its neighbour, as in the all-columns design picture.
  • Steps 9 and 10: the header labels keep the same size, weight and grey colour at Compact and at Comfortable.
  • Step 11: at 1536 px no header label touches or overlaps its neighbour.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10048 (Story 5, Choose what is shown), SV-10050 (Story 7, Line technicians), SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 52 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S5-R4, S7-R7, S2-R21 and Out of Scope (rank numbers; Collapse all and Expand all), read 14 Oct 2026; Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html", states core__work-orders__tech-regular__light__1440 and states__work-orders__tech-all-columns__light__1440 (design pictures DC-04-tech-view-header-row-1440.png, DC-04-tech-view-all-columns-1440.png, rendered from that export at the width in the name), read 14 Oct 2026. Covers the design defects SV-11317 (reported 14 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), SV-11321 (reported 14 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward). Where the PRD says nothing about the look, the design is the source. Source-verified 14 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build.

The design's header row reads "Unit #" and "Assigned Tech"; this case follows the PRD's "Unit" and "Assigned Techs" (question PQ-V03 to the product owner, not yet answered). The design's Tech View column chooser does not offer On Site, VIN/Serial # or Lead Technician; this case follows the PRD (question W-2, not yet answered).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R4: “Until the user changes Tech View’s columns, Tech View shows these columns, in this order, as in the design: Status, Waiting On Parts, Number, Customer, Unit, Asset, Progress, Service Advisor, Clocked In, Lines, Assigned Techs, Created on, Total price (Total price subject to financial permission). On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician are off by default; each can be added with the column chooser (S2-R4). List’s columns are unchanged.”
  • S7-R7: “In Tech View the Assigned Techs column sits immediately after Lines, matching the design. It is on by default (S5-R4) and can be removed through the column chooser (S2-R4).”
  • S2-R21: “Tech View’s column header labels are 12px, medium weight (500), in the secondary text color, as in the design. Labels never overlap a neighboring label.”
  • Out of Scope: “Rank numbers (1, 2, 3, and so on) beside each Tech View row, as the design shows.”
  • Out of Scope: “Collapse all and Expand all controls for the technician groups. Groups collapse one at a time (S2-R5, S2-R13).”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View column header row: “font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--sv-text-secondary); white-space: nowrap;”
